scope_note: Top-5 end-to-end Lamdera message flows (view click -> FrontendMsg -> update -> sendToBackend ToBackend -> Backend.updateFromFrontend -> GameLogic -> broadcast ToFrontend -> Frontend.updateFromBackend -> new view), including the two Random.generate async re-entries (InitializeGameAndTileDrawStackShuffled, TileDrawStackShuffled); low-priority flows (tile rotation, lobby kick/kill, mid-game rejoin) excluded beyond cross-references.

elements.name: Placing a tile on the board (turn step 1)
elements.description: Current player clicks a highlighted grid cell in PlaceTileState. Validity (empty cell adjacent to the grid, matching sideFeatures against N/E/S/W neighbours) is enforced ONLY client-side by FrontendHelpers; the server applies placeTile unconditionally (GameLogic docs: 'Does not check whether the move is valid'). placeTile renumbers sideIds, inserts the tile, merges adjacent features across tileGrid and meeple dict, and switches gameState to PlaceMeepleState. All clients converge via Lamdera broadcast. Initial state: gameState == PlaceTileState, currentPlayer owns the turn. Final states: PlaceMeepleState (happy path) or unchanged state on the three reject paths. No fork/join nodes: Elm update loops are sequential; the Lamdera broadcast is a single fan-out action on the external lane, and the acting client is expected to receive the same broadcast as every other client.

elements.label: End (no-op): backend model unchanged (Cmd.none), client never receives a reply

elements.name: Placing a meeple with immediate feature scoring (turn step 2)
elements.description: After placeTile, the same player may drop a meeple on a side/cloister of the last-placed tile or skip. Client offers only unoccupied sides (+ cloister center); if the player has 0 meeples left only Skip is offered. placeMeeple inserts the meeple, scores every newly FINISHED feature by tile count with a 2x bonus for completed cities (>2 tiles), adds cloister scores, awards points to majority owners, removes finished features from the meeple dict (returning those meeples), decrements the placer's meeple count (unless Skip), advances currentPlayer and sets PlaceTileState. The backend then issues Random.generate TileDrawStackShuffled (async re-entry): the shuffled draw stack either yields a playable tile (normal refill) or, if none exists, triggers finishGame (PR-5). Server never validates the position or the turn owner. Initial state: PlaceMeepleState with lastPlacedTile set. Final states: PlaceTileState with a fresh drawn tile, FinishedState, or unchanged state on the two no-op paths. No fork/join nodes: Elm updates are sequential; the broadcast is one fan-out action on the external lane.

elements.name: Any feature of the last-placed tile finished?
elements.label: Decision: do any sideIds of lastPlacedTile pass isFeatureFinished? (getTileSideIds lastPlacedTile |> Set.toList |> List.filter (isFeatureFinished game.tileGrid))
elements.description: isFeatureFinished: for every tile, each side carrying this sideId must have a neighbour tile on that side (and no cloister of that sideId). An empty filter result means nothing is scored this turn.

elements.name: Completed city with score > 2? (2x bonus)
elements.label: Decision (per finished feature): completed city with score > 2? (score > 2 && getSideIdFeature sideId game.tileGrid == City)
elements.description: Cities larger than 2 tiles give 2x points when completed before the game ends (code comment at GameLogic.elm:430).

elements.name: Score finished features + cloisters, award majority
elements.label: Score finished features: countFeature (number of tiles sharing the sideId) with 2x for qualifying cities; append cloister scores (getAdjacentTileCloisterScores: cloisters with all 8 neighbours, score 9); award each score to the majority owners via getFeatureOwners, accumulated into playerScores
elements.description: finishedFeatureScores feeds both the score dict and the finished-sideId list used for meeple removal/returns.

elements.name: Return meeples, advance turn, PlaceTileState
elements.label: Remove finished features from the meeple dict (those meeples are returned to their owners, +1 to playerMeeples); placer's meeple count -1 if position /= Skip else 0; currentPlayer <- getNextPlayer (wraps to 0); gameState <- PlaceTileState
elements.description: Meeple economy: 7 meeples each at start (Types/Game.elm:61); placed meeples are returned only when their feature finishes.

elements.name: Random cmd issued: TileDrawStackShuffled re-entry
elements.label: Async re-entry: Random.generate TileDrawStackShuffled (Random.List.shuffle updatedGame.tileDrawStack) - the Elm runtime executes the shuffle cmd, then the shuffled stack re-enters Backend.update as BackendMsg TileDrawStackShuffled
elements.description: This is a genuine asynchronous re-entry (Elm Cmd channel), not a sequential step: the turn is already advanced before the shuffle result arrives.

elements.name: Playable tile in shuffled draw stack?
elements.label: Decision (refill re-entry): does the shuffled draw stack yield a playable tile? (getPlayableTileFromDrawstack game.tileGrid shuffledTileDrawStack -> (Just nextTileId, drawStack) | (Nothing, _))
elements.description: getPlayableTileFromDrawstack pops tiles until one is placeable in at least one of 4 rotations (tileCanBePlacedAnywhere); (Nothing, []) when the stack is exhausted.

elements.name: Normal refill: new tileToPlace
elements.label: Normal refill: tileToPlace <- getTile nextTileId; tileDrawStack <- remaining (playable) tiles
elements.description: Unplaceable tiles at the top of the stack are skipped and dropped from the stack.

elements.name: No playable tile: finishGame (PR-5)

elements.name: Game initialization with shuffled tile draw (lobby -> game)
elements.description: Lobby-to-game transition. Any lobby player clicks 'Start'; the backend builds the game with initializeGame (71-tile draw stack from initializeDrawStack, starting grid with tile 0 at (0,0), 7 meeples per player, currentPlayer 0, PlaceTileState), switches BackendModel to BeGamePlayed and issues Random.generate InitializeGameAndTileDrawStackShuffled over the shuffled draw stack (async re-entry). On re-entry, getPlayableTileFromDrawstack skips unplaceable tiles to pick the FIRST playable tile (or falls back to tile 0 - 'First move should be always possible'), then broadcasts GameInitialized so every lobby client switches to the game view. Initial state: FeLobby / BePlayerRegistration with 1..5 registered players. Final state: BeGamePlayed with PlaceTileState and a drawn first tile, or unchanged state if the backend was not in the lobby. No fork/join nodes: Elm updates are sequential; broadcast is one fan-out action on the external lane.

elements.name: Player registration and lobby join
elements.description: A fresh client (init -> FePlayerRegistration on page load; the Lamdera ClientConnected hook only feeds lobby updates to already-registered clients) submits a name. Client-side: the trimmed name must be non-empty. Server-side: duplicate names are rejected (the requesting client is sent the EXISTING player list via sendToFrontend with no explicit error - it simply sees the unchanged lobby) and a full lobby (playerLimit = 5) is rejected with LobbyIsFull, which kicks the requesting client back to the registration form with a 'Lobby is full.' error and a 'Kill lobby' button. On success the player is appended and the updated list is broadcast to all clients, which re-render the lobby. Initial state: FePlayerRegistration. Final states: FeLobby with updated list (success / duplicate) or FePlayerRegistration with an error (empty name / lobby full). No fork/join nodes: Elm updates are sequential; sendToFrontend/broadcast are single fan-out actions on the external lane.

elements.description: The client optimistically leaves the form before the server answers.

elements.name: Does the name already exist?
elements.label: Decision (server): does the name already exist in the lobby? (List.member playerName players)
elements.description: Server-side duplicate check inside (RegisterPlayer, BePlayerRegistration).

elements.name: Duplicate name: rejected silently
elements.label: Duplicate name: model unchanged; sendToFrontend (ONLY the requesting client) PlayerRegistrationUpdated { players } - the client, already in FeLobby, is shown the existing player list with no explicit 'duplicate' error
elements.description: Error path: the rejection is visible only as 'the list did not change'; no dedicated error message exists for duplicates.

elements.name: Is the lobby full?
elements.label: Decision (server): would the lobby exceed the limit? (List.length newPlayers <= playerLimit where newPlayers = playerName :: players and playerLimit = 5)
elements.description: Server-side capacity check; the limit constant lives in Types/Game.elm.

elements.name: Registration accepted: append player
elements.label: Registration accepted: players <- playerName :: players; model stays BePlayerRegistration
elements.description: Happy path state change.

elements.name: Lobby full: send LobbyIsFull
elements.label: Lobby full: model unchanged (players stay at the limit); sendToFrontend (ONLY the requesting client) LobbyIsFull
elements.description: Error path: only the rejected client is informed.

elements.name: Lamdera broadcast PlayerRegistrationUpdated
elements.label: Lamdera broadcast (PlayerRegistrationUpdated { players = newPlayers }) to all connected clients
elements.description: Fans the new lobby list out to every connected client.

elements.name: Lobby clients update their player list
elements.label: All clients in FeLobby: updateFromBackend replaces FeLobby.players; lobby view re-renders the (updated) player list with a red 'kick' link per player and the 'Start' button
elements.description: Convergence point for lobby updates.

elements.name: Rejected client reverts to registration form
elements.label: Requesting client (in FeLobby when LobbyIsFull arrives): model <- FePlayerRegistration { nameInput = playerName, error = Just 'Lobby is full.' }; the registration view additionally renders a 'Kill lobby' button for this error
elements.description: The only place the FeKillLobby button appears; clicking it sends KillLobby (Frontend.elm:85-86), which empties the lobby server-side (Backend.elm:135-138).

elements.name: End (rejected client-side): empty name
elements.label: End (rejected client-side): 'Name cannot be empty.' shown; registration form stays
elements.description: Final state: FePlayerRegistration with error.

elements.name: End (duplicate): shown existing lobby list
elements.label: End (duplicate name): client stays in the lobby view showing the existing player list (the name was not added)
elements.description: Final state: FeLobby with the pre-existing list; no explicit duplicate error.

elements.name: End: registered in lobby
elements.label: End: player is registered - lobby view shows the updated list; 'Start' begins the game (PR-3)
elements.description: Final state: FeLobby with the new player appended.

elements.name: End (lobby full): error + Kill lobby button
elements.label: End (lobby full): 'Lobby is full.' error + 'Kill lobby' button shown in the registration form
elements.description: Final state: FePlayerRegistration with the full-lobby error.

elements.name: End-of-game final scoring
elements.description: Triggered inside the TileDrawStackShuffled re-entry (issued after every turn's meeple placement, see PR-2): when getPlayableTileFromDrawstack yields Nothing - the shuffled draw stack holds no tile that can be placed in any of 4 rotations - the backend runs finishGame instead of refilling. finishGame scores ALL still-open features (every sideId present in the meeple dict, via countFeature) and ALL cloisters (countCloister per cloister tile), awards them by majority (getFeatureOwners), empties the meeple dict and sets FinishedState; the finished game is broadcast like any UpdateGameState. The winner is NOT explicitly computed anywhere - final scores are simply displayed in the sidebar, so the winner is implicit (highest score). Afterward a client may click 'Terminate Game' to reset the backend to an empty lobby and return every client to the registration form. Initial state: BeGamePlayed mid-game, draw stack exhausted. Final states: BeGamePlayed/FinishedState (default) or BePlayerRegistration { players = [] } after TerminateGame. No fork/join nodes: Elm updates are sequential; broadcasts are single fan-out actions on the external lane.

lane_legend.client: Player's browser: src/Views/GameView.elm (FinishedState render + 'Terminate Game' button) and src/Frontend.elm (update / updateFromBackend / view).
lane_legend.server: Lamdera backend: src/Backend.elm update (Nothing branch of TileDrawStackShuffled) + src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm finishGame + src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm getPlayableTileFromDrawstack.
lane_legend.external: Lamdera platform + Elm runtime: the Random cmd / Cmd-channel re-entry that triggers this process (src/Backend.elm:177 -> 61) and the Lamdera broadcast fan-out (src/Backend.elm:6).
lane_legend.database: N/A - no database or persistence; all state lives in-memory in the Lamdera backend model (BackendModel, src/Types.elm:11-17).

error_paths: Alternate branch: the shuffled stack DOES contain a playable tile - normal refill, game continues instead of ending (src/Backend.elm:63-74)
Post-game: no winner is computed or announced; if no client terminates the game the FinishedState scoreboard simply remains (winner determination is display-only, src/Views/GameView.elm:694)

elements.name: Start: draw-stack re-entry with exhausted stack
elements.label: Start: BeGamePlayed; the BackendMsg TileDrawStackShuffled (issued after a turn's meeple placement) re-enters Backend.update with a shuffled draw stack
elements.description: Initial state: game mid-progress, currentPlayer just finished placing a meeple or skipping; the async shuffle cmd has completed.

elements.name: No playable tile in the draw stack?
elements.label: Decision: does the shuffled draw stack yield a playable tile? (getPlayableTileFromDrawstack game.tileGrid shuffledTileDrawStack -> (Just nextTileId, drawStack) | (Nothing, _))
elements.description: The (Nothing, _) arm is the game-over trigger: no remaining tile fits the board in any rotation.

elements.name: Playable tile: normal refill (game continues)
elements.label: Alternate branch: a playable tile exists - normal refill (tileToPlace <- getTile nextTileId; tileDrawStack <- rest; broadcast UpdateGameState) and the game continues (PR-2 happy path)
elements.description: The non-ending outcome of this decision.

elements.name: finishGame: score all open features
elements.label: finishGame step 1: score every still-open feature - for each sideId present in the meeple dict, (sideId, countFeature tileGrid sideId)
elements.description: Unlike in-turn scoring, ALL open features are scored here, not only finished ones (the board is done, so every feature counts).

elements.name: finishGame: score all cloisters
elements.label: finishGame step 2: score every cloister - for each placed tile with a cloister sideId, (sideId, countCloister) = number of the 8 surrounding tiles + 1
elements.description: Cloisters score 1 per adjacent tile (max 9).

elements.name: Award feature + cloister scores by majority
elements.label: finishGame step 3: award feature + cloister scores to the majority owners (getFeatureOwners per sideId) and accumulate into playerScores
elements.description: Ties are shared: every player with the maximum meeple count on the feature receives the full score.

elements.name: Empty meeple dict, FinishedState
elements.label: finishGame step 4: meeples <- Dict.empty; gameState <- FinishedState
elements.description: No winner is computed or stored - the finished game carries only playerScores; the winner is implicit (highest score) and only shown via the sidebar.
elements.unverified: Winner determination is inferred: there is no winner-calculation or announcement in the code, so 'the winner' is the player with the highest displayed final score (src/Views/GameView.elm:694).

elements.name: Lamdera broadcast UpdateGameState (finished game)
elements.label: Lamdera broadcast (UpdateGameState { game = finishedGame }) to all connected clients
elements.description: Same channel as in-turn updates - clients cannot distinguish 'finished' except via game.gameState.

elements.name: Clients apply the finished game
elements.label: All clients: updateFromBackend replaces FeGamePlayed.game with the finished game
elements.description: The (UpdateGameState, FeGamePlayed) convergence case.

elements.name: Render FinishedState: final board + final scores
elements.label: Render FinishedState: final board (no placeable overlay, no meeple overlay, tile preview = questionmark.png) + sidebar with final scores and remaining meeple counts per player; no further moves are possible
elements.description: The FinishedState branch renders the grid and sidebar only.

elements.name: Does a client send TerminateGame?
elements.label: Decision (server): does (TerminateGame, model) match (TerminateGame, BeGamePlayed _)? (client path: 'Terminate Game' button -> FeTerminateGame -> sendToBackend TerminateGame)
elements.description: Optional post-game cleanup; if no client ever clicks the button the game simply stays in FinishedState.

elements.name: Reset backend to empty lobby, broadcast GameTerminated
elements.label: Backend model <- BePlayerRegistration { players = [] }; Lamdera broadcast GameTerminated to all connected clients
elements.description: The finished game (and all scores) are discarded server-side.

elements.name: Clients return to registration form
elements.label: All clients: updateFromBackend (GameTerminated, FeGamePlayed _) -> model <- init (FePlayerRegistration { nameInput = '', error = Nothing })
elements.description: Back to the registration form for a potential next game.

elements.name: End (game continues): normal refill
elements.label: End (game continues): a playable tile was found - the turn loop continues with the newly drawn tile (PR-1/PR-2)
elements.description: Final state: BeGamePlayed with PlaceTileState.

elements.name: End: game stays FinishedState
elements.label: End: game remains in FinishedState - final scores stay displayed; no winner announcement is made (winner = implicit highest score)
elements.description: Final state: BeGamePlayed / FeGamePlayed with FinishedState, until someone terminates.
elements.unverified: The claim that no winner announcement exists is based on absence of such logic in the code (checked GameView sidebar and Game type).

elements.name: End: back to registration
elements.label: End: all clients return to the player registration form; backend is an empty lobby (BePlayerRegistration { players = [] })
elements.description: Final state: fresh registration form; a new game can start via PR-4 -> PR-3.

elements.name: N11 -> N15 (no termination)
elements.guard: no TerminateGame msg arrives - players keep viewing the FinishedState scoreboard

gaps: The draw stack has 71 tile ids per initializeDrawStack (src/Types/Game.elm:120-147), not the 74 stated in the planner brief - the evidence-based number (71) is used throughout.
No explicit winner determination exists: finishGame only fills playerScores (src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:511-556); the winner is implicit from the displayed scores (src/Views/GameView.elm:694).

Placement validity and turn ownership are enforced ONLY client-side (src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:48-110, src/Views/GameView.elm:58-75, 121-142); the server applies placeTile/placeMeeple without re-checking (docs at src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:311-322, 373-382) - a malicious client could place invalid moves or play out of turn.
Whether Lamdera `broadcast` also reaches the acting client is inferred from Lamdera broadcast semantics and the single-updateFromBackend client design; it is not verifiable from the repo alone.
Duplicate-name rejection has no explicit user-visible error message - the client only receives the unchanged player list (src/Backend.elm:99-102); modelled as a distinct end state with this caveat.

Low-priority flows not modelled as processes (per planner scope): tile rotation (src/Views/GameView.elm:740-742 + src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:21-40 + src/Backend.elm:150-158), lobby kick/kill (src/Backend.elm:125-138), rejoining an in-progress game (src/Backend.elm:120-123 + src/Frontend.elm:125-132); all remain cited where they touch modelled flows.
